art.subject: Red-throated Thrush (Turdus ruficollis), adult male in spring, as seen on Korean islands in April and May: plain ash-grey-brown crown, nape, back, wings and rump with no rufous tones, spots or scaling; a brick-red supercilium, and brick-red chin, throat, foreneck and upper breast forming a solid unmarked bib that ends cleanly on the breast; lores dusky grey; rest of the underparts whitish with a light grey wash on the breast sides and flanks; tail grey-brown in the centre with rufous outer feathers; bill dark grey with a yellow base to the lower mandible; dark brown eye; pale brown legs.
art.pose: standing upright on short grass at a woodland edge, side view, breast pushed forward between short runs
art.scene: Korean offshore island during spring migration in April: short grass and leaf litter at the edge of budding broadleaf woodland; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Medium-sized thrush, about the size of a Dusky Thrush and a little smaller and plumper than a Brown-eared Bulbul, with a shorter tail; rounded head and an upright stance on the ground with the breast pushed forward. Bill straight, a little shorter than the head. Legs medium length, pale brown. At rest the wingtips cover only the base of the tail; no wing-bars and no rufous wing panel. Tail medium length, square-ended, with rufous sides that show when it is spread on take-off. Underwing coverts orange-rufous in flight.
avoid: Do not paint rufous scaling or spots along the breast sides and flanks or a rufous wing panel; those are Naumann's Thrush (Turdus naumanni). This species has a solid red bib and plain wings.
Do not paint the bib black; a black throat and breast is Black-throated Thrush (Turdus atrogularis).
Do not paint dark spots or streaks on the adult male's red bib or on the whitish belly.
Do not paint a white supercilium or white throat on the male; both are brick-red.
